t: No appropriations in this title shall be available for hospitalization or examination of any persons (except beneficiaries entitled to such hospitalization or examination under the laws providing such benefits to veterans, and persons receiving such treatment under sections 7901 through 7904 of title 5, United States Code, or the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq.)), unless reimbursement of the cost of such hospitalization or examination is made to the “Medical Services” account at such rates as may be fixed by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

fable.w: This is an appropriations restriction that bars use of funds for hospitalization or examination of non-beneficiaries unless the cost is reimbursed. The tempting reading is that the Secretary's power to fix rates amounts to rulemaking, but the text does not call for regulations, public comment, a hearing, or consultation with anyone outside the federal government. The only decision-maker is a federal official acting alone, so no outside party takes part in a federal decision.
fable.s: at such rates as may be fixed by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs

opus.w: This is a limit on how appropriated money can be used: it bars spending on hospitalization or examination of non-beneficiaries unless the cost is reimbursed. The Secretary sets the reimbursement rates, but nothing here requires a comment period, a hearing, consultation with outside parties, or rulemaking. One could read the rate-setting as rulemaking authority like Example 6, but the text never says "by regulation." The only actor making a decision is a federal official.
opus.s: unless reimbursement of the cost of such hospitalization or examination is made to the “Medical Services” account at such rates as may be fixed by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a reimbursement requirement for medical services provided to veterans and other eligible persons. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The interaction is limited to financial transactions for services rendered, which falls under the exclusion for applications for benefits or grants/services.
qwen_chat.s: No appropriations in this title shall be available for hospitalization or examination of any persons... unless reimbursement of the cost of such hospitalization or examination is made to the “Medical Services” account at such rates as may be fixed by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "beneficiaries" or "persons" implies some form of interaction or participation. However, the text strictly concerns financial reimbursement mechanisms for medical services provided to specific groups. It does not describe any process where outside parties consult with, advise, or participate in a federal decision-making process. The interaction described is purely transactional (payment for services), not participatory in the sense of influencing a decision through consultation, comment, or advisory roles.
